thread:
marie: Heads-up — after shipping Apollo-7B (4-bit group=128) to the canary eval we’re seeing a spike in hallucinations on emoji-rich prompts. Samples attached. :eyes:

akshay: ugh. can you paste one of the failing prompts + model output? quick repro helps a lot.

marie: sure — root message timestamp: 1782301123. Example prompt:
```
User: Summarize this tweet:

\u201cHuge day 😅—released the new build! TL;DR?

#launchparty

Link: https://t.co/abc

\u201d

Apollo-7B (4-bit) output:
"The CEO announced that the company bought a rival, closing all stores in Europe."

FP16 baseline output:
"The team released a new build and celebrated — here's a short summary."
```

sara: interesting — that looks like a hallucination (incorrect factual claim). is this across many prompts or just these?

marie: eval-suite shows +11.8% hallucination rate vs FP16 on the "social-emoji" eval slice. total tokens similar. no obvious latency regressions.

ml-ci-bot: ATTENTION: eval-suite/regressions detected for model Apollo-7B quant=4bit. metric=hallucination_rate delta=+11.8% (p<0.01). job: nightly-evals/17823.

jon: two quick hypotheses: 1) quantization error interacting with tokenization boundaries (emoji / special unicode -> split tokens -> logit bias), 2) different preprocessing or normalization step slipped in when packaging the tokenizer for the new model.

tina: did we reuse the same tokenizer package as FP16? sometimes we have tokenizer v2 with NFKC normalization that collapses emoji variants. that can change token id alignment with pretrained weights.

marie: we built the model bundle with tokenizer v2.0.1 while FP16 uses v1.9.7. i thought they were compatible but i didn’t double-check normalization rules.

akshay: can you show the tokenized sequences for the prompt on both tokenizers + ids? a quick `tokenize()` diff will tell us if there's a shift.

marie: posted diffs:
```
# tokenizer v1.9.7: tokens = ['Huge', ' day', ' ', '\ud83d\ude05', '\u2014released', ' the', ' new', ' build', '!']
# ids = [10023, 45, 11, 5021, 32142, 66, 12, 934, 4]

# tokenizer v2.0.1: tokens = ['Huge', ' day', ' ', '\ud83d', '\ude05', '\u2014', 'released', ' the', ' new', ' build', '!']
# ids = [10023, 45, 11, 789, 1245, 302, 32142, 66, 12, 934, 4]
```

sara: aha — v2 splits the surrogate pair / emoji into two tokens (\ud83d + \ude05). that changes the KV cache alignment for early layers and could be worse under 4-bit quantization. FP16 was trained / evaluated with the paired token.

jon: that’s a plausible root cause. quantization reduces margin and small tokenization shifts can push decoding to different branches. two followups: (a) test Apollo-7B with tokenizer forced to v1 tokenization, (b) run a small head-to-head between 8-bit and 4-bit to see if error scales with bitwidth.

marie: running quick experiments now. command i used for tokenization check:
```bash
python - <<PY
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tokv1 = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/v1.json')
tokv2 = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/v2.json')
text = 'Huge day 😅—released the new build! TL;DR?'
print(tokv1.encode(text).tokens)
print(tokv2.encode(text).tokens)
PY
```

ml-ci-bot: experiment start: eval/1782301123/run-1 (compare-tokenizers). status=running.

tina: while that runs: if bundling used the wrong tokenizer we should be careful — customers hitting hosted API could see misaligned probabilities. recommend canary rollback to FP16 on the user-facing canary for immediate mitigation.

deploy-bot: initiating canary rollback: deploy/dedicated-a1-canary -> Apollo-7B@fp16 (request by tina). ETA ~6m.

akshay: also try re-quantizing with symmetric per-channel instead of per-tensor for attention layers — sometimes helps when token boundaries shift.

marie: quick results:
- tokenizer forced to v1 -> hallucination_rate drops back near baseline (delta +1.2%).
- re-quantize 8-bit -> no significant regression. 4-bit per-channel improved but still +3.4%

sara: that pretty much confirms a tokenization/quantization interaction. plan: (1) repackage Apollo-7B bundle to include tokenizer v1 compatibility shim, (2) re-run full nightly with 4-bit per-channel and group_size variations, (3) publish a short postmortem and update onboarding checklist to include tokenizer-compatibility check for quantized builds.

jon: also add an automated tokenization-diff test to the evals harness: for a small representative corpus check that token ids are identical or within epsilon mapping for new tokenizer versions. block quantized rollout if mismatch > threshold.

marie: will open PRs for (1)+(3) and start the longer nightly runs. thanks all. :pray:

deploy-bot: canary rollback complete: dedicated-a1-canary -> Apollo-7B@fp16 (status=success).

akshay: nice recovery. when you open the PR, tag me and i'll help with the per-channel quant configs.

marie: will do. adding follow-up action items to the intake ticket. thread end.
